issues.reason: The Existential section reserves the bare class symbol for a non-specific / generic object and directs a definite or possessed NP ('its highest alert') to a typed individual sk_<class>_<n>, so the bare constant violates a stated rule.
Possessive / genitive NP requires a possessive pronoun to attach its possessor by PartOf or Possession, and 'its' was dropped entirely, losing the force-alert link the text states.

The inconsistency stands — Names and casing lemmatizes adjectives inflectionally ('taller' -> 'tall'), so the class symbol must be high_alert to match its genus `high` — but the complaint that the superlative degree goes unrecorded is the reviewer's own attributive-superlative coverage gap, not a defect.

gaps_confirmed: an attributive superlative inside an NP ('its highest alert') — Comparatives & degree provides only the predicative (Most <scale> X <class>) and the comparative forms, so a superlative modifier has no carrier and is lost on lemmatization
a performative / journalistic 'can' ('The Telegraph can reveal that …'), which is not a capability claim about the subject but is stored as (Can e)
new_gaps: a possessed abstract level or setting ('placed his force on its highest alert') — Possession is the only available head, but the alert level is neither owned nor a component, so the possessive is recorded only by the opaque catch-all
repair_summary: Replaced the bare class constant highest_alert with a typed witness sk_alert_1 in the On oblique, at top level and inside the sealed Theme term alike; added (Member sk_alert_1 high_alert) and (Possession sk_alert_1 sk_force_1) to carry the definite NP and its dropped 'its' possessor; lemmatized the compound and its decomposition to high_alert, so (Inheritance high_alert alert) and (Inheritance high_alert high) now agree with the symbol.
notes: Because 'reveal' was routed as factive, the On atom appears both in the seal and at top level and had to change in both places. The superlative content is dropped rather than replaced by an invented carrier, per the attributive-superlative gap.
